evidence: LM_OPTIMIZER_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 permits a non-loopback bind while all 62 routes remain unauthenticated.
State-changing endpoints include apply, restore, save-default and delete.

issues.summary: Defensive broad catches hide failures in service code
issues.suggestion: Replace copied catches with one logged best-effort helper and let unexpected exceptions propagate; keep only documented tolerances.
evidence: optimizer.py contains 41 'except ...: pass' blocks, routes.py 30, cli/main.py 14.
Many wrap optional enrichment/persistence rather than documented tolerances.

issues.summary: Docstrings on long functions describe only one responsibility
issues.suggestion: Either split the function so the docstring is accurate, or expand it to list all side effects and outputs.
evidence: save_best_report is documented as saving a report but also builds diagnostics, presets and ladder sections.
_test_config documents loading but also benchmarks, scores and cleans up.

issues.summary: discovery/inspector.py still uses the legacy api/client instead of the service client
issues.suggestion: Port inspector.py to the service client and delete api/client.py once tests stop importing it.
evidence: inspector.py imports LMStudioClient, LoadConfig and ModelInfo from api.client.
The current host client lives in services/lm_studio.py.

issues.summary: Hardware scripts sit at the repository root instead of with the hardware package or tools
issues.suggestion: Move them under tools/ (or lm_optimizer/hardware/) and update entrypoints/README references.
evidence: Both root files have low fan-in and import lm_optimizer.services/domain.
The hardware package already owns detection and monitoring.

issues.summary: services/ is a flat directory mixing unrelated capabilities
issues.suggestion: Split into capability subpackages and keep a small services/__init__ facade for compatibility.
evidence: The directory contains orchestration, benchmark execution, reporting, host defaults, sandboxing and recommendation logic.
There are no subpackages to signal ownership.

issues.summary: tools/ mixes durable utilities with one-off campaign scripts
issues.suggestion: Move one-off scripts to tools/archive/ with a README, and rename durable tools by action (validate_live.py, audit_webui.py).
evidence: 39 scripts include reusable probes (live_validation, webui_audit) and dated campaign slices (speed16k_part2, speed16k_remaining_rerun).
No README or naming rule distinguishes them.

issues.summary: API routes keep current optimizer/run in module-level globals
issues.suggestion: Move current-run state into app.state or a small RunRegistry created in the lifespan hook and injected via dependency.
evidence: _current_optimizer and _current_run_id are assigned inside request handlers and read by later requests.
The scan reports 5 mutations of module-level state in this file.

issues.summary: api/main.py rewrites the route table at import time
issues.suggestion: Use a supported include_router pattern, move optional routers into a registration function called from the lifespan hook, and assert the final route table in a test.
evidence: Lines 63-106 manually recreate and filter APIRoutes because include_router was reported broken.
Late imports inside the module add hidden initialization order.

issues.summary: Command functions own several distinct responsibilities
issues.suggestion: Extract a shared optimization workflow service and keep CLI commands as thin adapters that parse input and render results.
evidence: optimize/auto combine argument validation, preflight, host lifecycle, run execution and report rendering.
The same responsibilities are also implemented in the API path.

issues.summary: _test_config combines load, benchmark, quality and persistence
issues.suggestion: Split into load_candidate, measure_candidate, evaluate_candidate and record_candidate steps composed by _test_config.
evidence: The 244-line function loads a model, runs cases, evaluates quality, records results and cleans up in one body.
Failure handling for each stage is interleaved.

issues.summary: Public helpers annotated -> dict return different key sets by branch
issues.suggestion: Return Pydantic models or TypedDicts with required/optional fields, and keep raw dicts only at serialization boundaries.
evidence: Several handlers and default helpers return dict with optional keys added conditionally.
Callers use .get(...) because the annotation does not promise a shape.

issues.summary: Docstrings describe the happy path but omit raised errors
issues.suggestion: Add Raises/Returns sections for public functions and align annotations with every return path.
evidence: Client methods raise on transport errors without a documented Raises section.
Some service helpers return None/False for invalid input instead of raising.

issues.summary: Retry and fallback branches repeat load/benchmark logic with slightly different guards
issues.suggestion: Extract a single attempt function returning an outcome and drive retries from one loop with an explicit retry policy.
evidence: LM Studio load fallback checks response, then polls loaded instances, then re-raises with a different message.
Benchmark reasoning fallback runs the same case twice with a conditional keep.

issues.summary: Long functions make the success condition hard to locate
issues.suggestion: Extract a small is_successful(run) predicate and use it at each decision point; keep rendering separate from decision logic.
evidence: The command bodies and report builder have several early returns and nested conditionals spread over hundreds of lines.
A reader must scan the whole body to know when a run is considered successful.

issues.summary: Some async functions perform no awaits
issues.suggestion: Convert purely synchronous handlers to def, or add a real await (e.g. asyncio.to_thread) for blocking work.
evidence: Several async handlers only call synchronous repository/template helpers.
They could be plain def handlers, which would let FastAPI run them in a threadpool.

issues.summary: Most service parameters and returns lack annotations
issues.suggestion: Annotate public entrypoints first (prepare_run, execute, run_cases, auto_run) with concrete types and enable mypy/pyright on those modules.
evidence: The AST census finds 693 unannotated parameters and 264 unannotated returns.
Public service methods accept advanced settings and config fragments as bare dicts.

issues.summary: dict[str, Any] is used where a concrete shape is known
issues.suggestion: Define TypedDicts (or dataclasses) for the LM Studio defaults document, duel payload and host guard state.
evidence: lmstudio_defaults.py has 23 dict[str, Any] annotations for a JSON document with known keys.
Key strings are repeated across merge/apply/diff functions.

issues.summary: Raw string literals bypass phase/stage/status enums
issues.suggestion: Normalize input once into enum members (parse_phase_skips) and compare enums internally; keep strings only at CLI/JSON boundaries.
evidence: The enum bypass census reports 30 comparisons against raw strings.
Skip-phase handling compares strings such as 'quality' instead of OptimizationPhase members in places.

add.description: backends/base.py defines BackendClient and assert_conforms, and OllamaClient implements the seam; backend-specific code is not spread through the domain.
web_main.py launches api.main:app, and ui/web.py is explicitly marked as deprecated reference code, so the current entrypoint is unambiguous.
The deprecated ui/web.py docstring names api.main:app as authoritative, which prevents a new engineer from wiring the wrong app.
OptimizationPhase/OptimizationStage enumerate the pipeline stages instead of relying on implicit string flow, which gives the orchestration a readable spine.
1,666 detected names across all packages use snake_case, so lexical convention is not a source of friction.
Most test modules are named after the production module they cover, which makes coverage discovery predictable.
BenchmarkService records success=False and an error per case instead of aborting the whole sweep, which keeps one bad prompt from losing a run.
Cancellation paths explicitly checkpoint state before unwinding, preserving recoverability across failures.
Terms such as run, configuration, phase, winner and ladder are used consistently across CLI, API and services, so domain names transfer between layers.
The BackendClient protocol is implemented by OllamaClient and exercised by conformance checks, so the abstraction has more than one consumer.
Functions such as parse_phase_skips and compose_granular_skips encode real skip semantics rather than forwarding arguments.
One HTTP client (httpx), one settings stack (pydantic-settings) and one CLI/UI stack (Typer/Rich + FastAPI) avoid duplicate-purpose libraries.
Helpers such as _looks_incomplete, _sample_mem and _extract_mtp_metrics are short, side-effect-light and easy to test.
The optimizer exposes ordered phases and skip names, so the CLI/API handoff for phase control is at least named and testable.
About 1,490 tests run in roughly five minutes, covering phases, scoring, persistence and CLI/UI parity.

add.header: Targeted regression tests for live findings
add.description: Load-response loss, echo-probe cleanup and context-speed ladder retries each gained a dedicated test after being found live.
Run, settings, compare, sandbox and judge endpoints use Pydantic response models, giving the most important payloads a stable schema.
The web UI binds 127.0.0.1 by default and CORS allows only localhost origins, reducing accidental network exposure.
The 2.5% comment ratio and short docstrings avoid restating code; comments generally explain constraints or intent.
web_main.py launches api.main:app and the deprecated module points to it, so the target of the migration is unambiguous.
domain, storage, backends, benchmark and scoring are named by responsibility, so the main layout is self-explanatory.
pydantic-settings provides one typed config object with environment support, avoiding scattered os.environ reads in most modules.
The FastAPI app uses a lifespan context for startup/shutdown work, giving a clear place for future initialization.
AdaptiveOptimizer runs named phases (speed, context speed, quality, recovery, validation) with explicit skip handling, which is a coherent orchestration spine.
Core domain dataclasses expose to_dict/from_dict pairs and are exercised by round-trip tests, giving persistence a reliable contract.
CLI and API helpers commonly validate inputs and return/raise early, keeping the happy path visible in short functions.
Domain dataclasses and Pydantic schemas type the main entities (runs, configs, metrics, requests), giving the persistence and HTTP layers a reliable core.
